judgments.comparative_verdict: Both reports hit all four expectations with equivalent grounding and depth; they are comparable.

report_1.evidence: A clinic that has never opened the setting WILL have reminders sent automatically — the flag defaults to enabled when unset.** The deciding code is the function `auto_send_reminders_enabled` in `backend/app/feature_flags.py`: line 11 checks `if tenant.settings.get("auto_send_reminders") is None:` and line 12 — the exact line that decides this case — is `return True`.

report_2.evidence: A clinic that has never opened this setting WILL have reminder messages sent automatically.** The deciding code is `auto_send_reminders_enabled` in `slotwise/backend/app/feature_flags.py:10-13`. For a never-touched clinic, `tenant.settings` has no `auto_send_reminders` key, so `tenant.settings.get("auto_send_reminders")` is `None`; the check at `feature_flags.py:11`... is true and **line 12 (`return True`) decides it**

report_1.evidence: for this feature, default-on for an unset value is the wrong behavior... I would change `backend/app/feature_flags.py:12` from `return True` to `return False`

report_2.evidence: for this flag, the default is wrong and should be inverted to off... I would change `feature_flags.py:12` from `return True` to `return False`

report_1.evidence: created `feature_flags.py` with one function, `compact_calendar_view_enabled`... added `auto_send_reminders_enabled` as a structurally identical, line-for-line copy of the function directly above it... defaulting a display preference on affects only pixels, while defaulting auto-messaging on silently opts every existing tenant into sending SMS/email to patients

report_2.evidence: `compact_calendar_view_enabled` (`feature_flags.py:4-7`) defaults on appropriately: it's a UI preference... appended `auto_send_reminders_enabled` directly beneath it as a line-for-line structural copy... the two flags sit in opposite risk categories — a cosmetic view preference versus an automated outbound action toward patients

report_1.evidence: Add a global kill switch.** The grep confirmed the per-tenant flag at `reminders.py:25` is the *only* gate — there is no environment-level or ops-level way to stop all sends quickly if the job misbehaves

report_2.evidence: Add an environment-level master switch** ANDed with the per-tenant value... there is currently **no kill switch**: disabling the feature fleet-wide would require editing every tenant's settings row
